prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

"Avocado Green Mattress was cofounded by Jeff D'Andrea, Dan D'Andrea, Jay Decker, and Mark Abrials. That experience shaped the brand's commitment to independent certification, public verification, and radical transparency about materials and manufacturing. When was Avocado Green Mattress founded? [P4] source: https://www.avocadogreenmattress.com/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 2014, 2016, 2018 | published: unknown
"The Avocado brand launched in 2016 and merged with Brentwood Home in 2018. Is Avocado a B Corp? Yes. [P5] source: https://www.avocadogreenmattress.com/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"OUR BRAND MISSION: ORGANIC, SAFE, & RESPONSIBLE Avocado mattresses are designed in Hoboken and handmade in our GOTS-certified factory in Fullerton, California, with domestic and imported certified organic materials. Our mission is to be the most trusted source for certified organic mattresses, pillows, and bedding at accessible prices — while holding ourselves to verified environmental, ethical, and social standards across our entire supply chain."

[P6] source: https://avocadogreenmattress.ca/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Natural, Organic, & Beyond Our mission is to be one of the world’s most sustainable brands. Our green mattresses and bedding are certified organic and non-toxic. Our factory and wood shop in Los Angeles are GOTS organic and FSC® certified — and powered entirely by renewable energy. We are the world’s only Climate Neutral Certified® mattress and bedding brand. Most of our products are Greenguard Gold and MADE SAFE® certified. We donate one percent of all revenues to environmental nonprofits through our membership with 1% For The Planet."

[P7] source: https://www.avocadogreenmattress.com/pages/news | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 2020 | published: unknown
"Newly Certified B Corp Avocado Mattress Launches Memorial Day Sale on Organic Mattresses MAY 8, 2020 ## Sustainable Mattress Maker Avocado Green Launches New Organic Crib Mattress APRIL 22, 2020"

[P8] source: https://help.avocadogreenmattress.com/en/articles/4649949-who-makes-avocado-mattresses | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Who Makes Avocado Mattresses? Avocado does. Every Avocado organic mattress is hand-needle-tufted by skilled bedmakers in our own GOTS-certified manufacturing facility in Fullerton, California — not by a contract manufacturer or a third-party factory shared with other brands. That distinction matters more than it might seem. Many direct-to-consumer mattress brands are marketing and logistics operations: they design products, build websites, and manage customer relationships, but the mattresses themselves are made by contract manufacturers who produce for multiple brands simultaneously. Avocado is a bedmaker."

[P9] source: https://avocadogreenmattress.ca/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"A Force for Good Avocado is a Certified B Corporation®, a new kind of business that balances purpose and profit. We are legally required to consider the impact of our decisions on our workers, customers, suppliers, community, and the environment. B Corporations are a community of leaders, driving a global movement of people using business as a force for good."

[P10] source: https://avocadogreenmattress.ca/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"TO BE A TRULY SUSTAINABLE BRAND Now, we're raising the bar for what it means to be a sustainable brand. We’re a certified B Corp and Climate Neutral certified. Plus, we donate 1% of revenues to vetted nonprofits through our commitment to 1% For the Planet. Our products are organic certified by GOTS. We don’t use toxic chemicals. Our factories are powered by renewable energy and are approaching zero waste. We even care for nearly 200,000 sheep and grow and produce our own natural latex from our own farms. And the journey has just begun."
